title: Can Steam/players detect AI textures?
author: GhostGuyBroke
selftext: Is there any way for an AI-generated texture to be detected as AI?

comments.author: DashLego
comments.body: It depends of how generic is your assets, the most generic ones has an AI look that everyone that has worked with AI can recognize

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
Here is a trick, learn how to bake textures in your 3D software, if you don't have 3D software yet Blender is an good choice and free.

Then instead of generating AI textures generate 3D models to make the textures you need. For example if you need rocks, you can use AI to generate 3D rocks. Then in your 3D software use the materials and lights, to make some changes, and finally bake your textures. Doing this removes the distinctive AI noise pattern, and even allows you more control, and gives you all the texture maps you want.

Of course, there is still an chance an AI detector will say it is AI, but even the best AI detectors give a large amount of false positives.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
Texture baking is just one more trick where users use 3D models to make textures, this is actually widely used in AAA development, alongside procedural textures etc.

So for example these images was from me explaining tiling texture baking an while back: [https://i.imgur.com/S5JBhUP.png](https://i.imgur.com/S5JBhUP.png) \-> [https://i.imgur.com/92sjW2k.png](https://i.imgur.com/92sjW2k.png)

3D modeling is an vector art form, so here is me making some vector art sample textures: [https://imgur.com/a/9ZzhNlD](https://imgur.com/a/9ZzhNlD) \-> [https://imgur.com/a/lgTdx4M](https://imgur.com/a/lgTdx4M) \-> [https://imgur.com/a/sjWjeie](https://imgur.com/a/sjWjeie) These are used for plotting texel density.

When it is stylized you can easily tell it was made using 3D: [https://www.blenderkit.com/asset-gallery-detail/97b171b4-2085-4c25-8793-2bfe65650266/](https://www.blenderkit.com/asset-gallery-detail/97b171b4-2085-4c25-8793-2bfe65650266/) (not mine) but an artist that can make realistic looking models has no problem with textures, and AI makes it even easier.

comments.author: loopywolf
comments.body: Well, from a very high level perspective, humans have already become good at detecting AI artwork and text.  In the case of textures, I would say it has a lot to do with how often it is repeated, e.g. some water textures look great, but if they are repeated 100x across the screen, you can easily spot the pattern.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
AI textures are pretty low quality when examined at any reasonable distance. You can generate some reasonable noise or painterly patterns and get away with it, but full object or character textures, or realistic/clean styles are out of the question unless you are knowledgeable enough to make significant clean up efforts.

If you mean automated detection, I'm not sure. Depends on how they were generated. I've never really cared about artificial detection. What I'd be concerned with is whether its slop enough for someone to look at and identify as AI genned due to quality control issues. In my experience, it takes as much effort to clean up said textures to be usable as it does to just paint my models and bake them (as others have suggested). But I use cel-shading/flat colors so the painting process is quite simple in my case. I definitely see some value in utilizing a more chaotic painterly style where you might be able to get away with an AI generated base. Might be fine with abstract styles too. Don't worry so much about people "detecting" it. Just make a good game.  Be honest about your product. If people hate on it that's on them. 

I create all of my game's art, but I will still happily disclose that I've used AI thoroughly in the creation process (coding, concepting, etc... refactoring alone has saved me countless hours.) If people choose not to play it due to that, it's on me for not making a good enough game that they overlooked any illogical prejudices they might otherwise have had.

People seem to think that games being AI are stopping people from playing them. Outside of rare instances like youtubers brigading against those games and causing some level of review bombing, the people not playing  these games would not be playing them anyway. These people aren't looking at the game and going, "Damn that game looks like so much  fun!  Wait, they used AI in its creation? Those fucking scumbags, what is this trash" Rather they're either already  opposed to the game's appearance / indifferent to it, and the usage of AI in some part of the process is simply something for them to grasp onto and  rally against without looking like buffoons in their social sphere. If they go off on some game they think looks like shit where someone hand drew a bunch of stick figures, they'd look like an ass that's cyber-bullying someone for a lack of talent. Really it just comes down to them viewing one thing as an acceptable reason to justify cyber-bullying, and another they know they'd be considered a villain for doing the same thing.

comments.author: q_OwO_p
comments.body:
Most AI puts watermark all over the image it generates

If you zoom in a lot on a ChatGPT generated image for example you can see a bunch of pixels in a pattern, it’s easiest to see the watermarks if you tell it to generate solid color.

With Gemini its watermark is very noticeable if you’re an artist because it reduces the quality of the image a lot and makes it very noisy, if you feed it an image for example at 1080x1080 res (max res) then tell it to make no changes, the generated image you can easily notice side by side especially the more you zoom in that it looks blurry and everything’s quality is reduced like there’s invisible noise all over the image.

AI are using all of these methods to watermark images, and I’m sure big companies have deals with AI producers that allow them to identify AI images.

I tried to see if I could fool Gemini that an art it generated wasn’t generated by it by scanning with its synthID and it only worked when I edited them image to be super blurry that it was essentially splotches blurry of color and when I made the color palette of the image just pure black and white, that was the only ways it couldn’t tell that it generated the asset.

So basically, just assume they will know even if your art doesn’t obviously look like AI.

I’m sure Steam’s going to implement AI scanning tools in review process any month now for games and the AI will automatically check these things and more about the game…
